changes.reason: No Gaussian elimination: one linear congruence per biconnected block fixes S, then the core is constructing 'transfers' between spanning trees along DFS base cycles (tutorial).
Solving (k-1)S = T mod p per block is a linear congruence mod p.
Tutorial uses no hashing: merge collinear segments, rotate by 45/90/180, translate and compare sorted segment sets; it is a careful-implementation geometry problem.
The solution itself is deterministic apart from the hash; the tool to know is set hashing (sum of random values via prefix sums). Randomness is a property of the input.
Follows the primary swap; the probabilistic root argument stays as secondary.
No step-by-step greedy: the answer is the count of adjacent non-consecutive ranks (forced splits) plus n+s-1 combines, a pure counting observation.
Textbook 'lower bound max(colorful rows, colorful cols) + construction that reaches it', which is exactly the constructive topic's description.
The crux is the run-length characterization (runs shrink, a 0 can swallow 1-runs); the single pointer during greedy matching is incidental.
The symmetric run check is a trivial loop over runs; no palindrome algorithm (Manacher/KMP) needed.
No divisors or sieve: the bound is just k*f_1 <= n (brute-force amortized bound already covers it).
Counts multiset orderings (factorial number system); no permutation cycles or functional graph involved.
Balanced group sizes come from convexity of x(x-1)/2, not from ordering by a key; closed-form lists convexity.
The hull of lattice points under y=floor(d*i/hp) is found with continued fractions (Euclid-like), a needed technique named in the key idea.

topic_notes.note: 'canonical form' in includes pulls in problems that canonicalize and compare sorted sets without any hashing (nerc2024-G). Consider moving 'canonical form' out or saying 'forma canônica + hash' explicitly.
'linear algebra mod p' attracted nerc2022dec-J, which needs only one linear congruence. Reserve it for real Gaussian elimination / basis / rank problems (apac2024-L fits).

Becoming a catch-all for 'math with a formula': water-filling convex optimization (nerc2022apr-B), sign assignment of |x_i - x_j| (nerc2025-E), cycle recurrence with a free parameter (nerc2025-G), inequalities (nerc2025-A). Acceptable, but a 'convexity / convex optimization (marginal equalization, slope trick, convex hull of prefix sums)' topic would better serve nerc2022apr-B, nerc2022apr-H and nerc2023-B if other scopes show more of these.

Pure implementation problems are scattered across parsing-brackets (nerc2021-A, nerc2024-E) and hashing (nerc2024-G). Renaming to 'Implementação/simulação cuidadosa' would give them a clear home and make the topic's stats more meaningful.

Cactus graphs recur almost every NERC (2019-C, 2021-C, 2022dec-C, 2023-C, 2024-C, 2025-C) plus apac2025-C; they are split between dfs-tree-bridges and graph-constructive by primary. Consider naming 'cactos' in the dashboard topic name so this recurring NERC theme shows up.
Use for algorithms that randomize themselves (nerc2022dec-A, nerc2021-I). Random input with deterministic hashing (nerc2022dec-B) belongs under hashing.

raw_notes.note: candidate_tags list 'hashing', but the tutorial uses none: merge consecutive same-direction segments, rotate by 45/90/180, translate so the smallest endpoint matches, and compare sorted segment sets. Replace 'hashing' with 'implementation'.

candidate tag 'linear algebra mod p' overstates it: the algebra is one congruence (n_block-1)*S = T mod p per biconnected block. The rest is constructive transfers (+x on T1, -x on T2 = T1 - e1 + e2) along DFS base cycles, processed by decreasing depth.
